description: Compute rise, set, and culmination (transit) times for a body at an observer location, plus the maximum altitude at culmination. For the Sun, also returns the three twilight pairs (civil −6°, nautical −12°, astronomical −18°) so a single call answers "when does the sun set and when is it truly dark." Each pair covers the night after the cycle's set — dusk that evening, dawn the next morning — so the dawn listed beside a sunrise is the following day's; for the dawn before a sunrise, read the previous cycle or start a day earlier. Searches forward from `start` (default today) and returns the next `count` cycles (default 1). When the body is already above the horizon at `start`, the first cycle is the interval in progress: its `set` is the imminent one and its `rise` is null, since that rise precedes the search — so a set is never reported earlier than the rise beside it. Circumpolar or never-rises situations are reported as null rise/set fields with an explanatory note rather than an error — the fact is the answer. Default elevation is 0 m; pass an IANA `timezone` for observer-local times. This server does not geocode — resolve coordinates upstream first.

body.description: The body to compute rise/set for. Twilight is included only when this is "sun".

count.description: Number of forward rise/set cycles to return. Default 1, max 31.

elevation.description: Observer elevation in meters above sea level. Default 0.

latitude.description: Observer latitude in decimal degrees, north positive.

longitude.description: Observer longitude in decimal degrees, east positive.

start.description: Search start as an ISO 8601 UTC string, e.g. "2024-06-21T00:00:00Z". Defaults to now. A value with no zone designator is read as UTC, not the local zone of the server process.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for localized output, e.g. "America/Los_Angeles". When omitted, output is UTC-only.

name: astronomy_get_rise_set

body.description: The body these rise/set cycles are for, echoed from the request.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_time`: The `start` value is not a parseable ISO 8601 instant, or names a calendar date that does not exist (e.g. 2026-02-30). `time_out_of_range`: The requested start instant is outside the engine's high-accuracy span (≈1900–2100). `invalid_timezone`: The `timezone` value is not an IANA zone this runtime knows. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

events.description: One entry per rise/set/transit cycle, searching forward from the start time.

items.description: One rise/set/transit cycle, with twilight when the body is the Sun.

note.description: Explanatory note when a rise or set is absent (e.g. "Circumpolar — never sets at this latitude/date.").

rise_local.description: Rise time in observer-local time, present only when a timezone was supplied.

rise_utc.description: Rise time in ISO 8601 UTC, or null when the body does not rise in this cycle — because it is circumpolar, or because it was already above the horizon at the search start, whose rise precedes the search. The accompanying note says which.

set_local.description: Set time in observer-local time, present only when a timezone was supplied.

set_utc.description: Set time in ISO 8601 UTC, or null when the body does not set in this cycle.

transit_altitude_degrees.description: Maximum altitude in degrees at culmination, or null when not found.

transit_local.description: Culmination time in observer-local time, present only when a timezone was supplied.

transit_utc.description: Culmination (highest point) time in ISO 8601 UTC, or null when not found.

twilight.description: The three twilight pairs, present only when body is "sun". Each pair spans one night: dusk is the evening of this cycle's set and dawn is the following morning, so a cycle's dawn falls a day after its rise. The dawn before a given sunrise is in the previous cycle's pair — start the search a day earlier to get it.

astronomical.description: Astronomical twilight (Sun at −18°): dusk and the following dawn, bounding the dark-sky window.

dawn_local.description: Dawn in observer-local time — the morning after the cycle's set — present only when a timezone was supplied.

dawn_utc.description: Dawn (Sun ascending through the depth) in ISO 8601 UTC, or null if it does not occur. This is the morning after the cycle's set, ending the night that begins at the dusk beside it — a day later than the cycle's rise, not the dawn before it.

dusk_local.description: Dusk in observer-local time — the evening of the cycle's set — present only when a timezone was supplied.

dusk_utc.description: Dusk (Sun descending through the depth) in ISO 8601 UTC, or null if it does not occur. This is the evening of the cycle's set.
